item.title: If I Were Starting A Software Engineering Career Today
item.description: If I Were Starting A Software Engineering Career Today I’ve been writing software professionally for over a decade now, and during that time I’ve taken part in hiring many other talented software engineers. So when I hear new graduates and junior developers express fear or frustration about finding a job in today’s economic climate, I stop and think about what I would do if I were starting my career today.

item.title: Give youself more space to think
item.description: Give yourself more space to think Sometimes it’s nice to drastically simplify the tools you use in an attempt to free up mental space. Like Luke Skywalker disabling his targeting device in order to fire a precise shot into the Death Star. Try disabling autocomplete on your code editor, and use just one monitor. Close as many windows as you can, and only check chat and/or email at pre-determined times. You may find that without a bunch of distracting “help” popping up as you type, you’ll be free to think and write code in a clearer, more contiguous headspace.

item.title: Is your startup a rocket ship or a tree?
item.description: Is your startup a rocket ship or a tree? Rocket ships require an immense amount of funding and expertise, and even then, they tend to explode before getting very far off the ground. When they do manage to make it to space, they jettison everything that got them there in order to propel a tiny payload at the top further. Trees require little more than a tiny seed and consistent cultivation.
